title: Seoul Concept Book — Idol Grid Photobook
description: A K-pop mini-album slide that pairs dual-script group naming (Hangul above, Latin below at equal weight) with a 3–4 member concept-photo grid, an oversized centered album title in heavy sans-serif, and a tracked-monospace tracklist footer — closer to a HYBE photobook spread than a conventional deck slide.
philosophy: This template exists for the precise, fashion-forward visual language of contemporary K-pop art direction: bilingual parity is non-negotiable, and cool-toned whitespace is trusted to do the emotional lifting that other templates offload to decoration. It refuses hierarchy between scripts — Hangul and Latin stand at equal optical weight because neither identity is secondary. Every structural choice mirrors a real album booklet convention, so the speaker inhabits the role of creative director rather than presenter. It is built for audiences who read design decisions.
goodFor: K-pop group concept or debut introduction slides
Music label artist showcase and A&R pitch decks
Fan event program visuals built around member photo grids
Entertainment industry pitches requiring album-booklet visual credibility
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly financial or business reviews
Academic research, thesis, or policy presentations
Corporate compliance and legal briefing decks
Western brand identity presentations with no Korean pop-culture connection
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the opening gatefold of a prestige K-pop photobook — cool, deliberate, and fashion-editorial in restraint. Drama is entirely structural: a wall of high-concept member portraits drops sharply into a field of icy whitespace where the group identity and album title hold the silence. Bilingual script parity reads as an intentional design manifesto rather than a label obligation, and the monospace footer signals catalog credibility. Avoid warmth, decorative motifs, or any softening element that undermines the cool authority of a creative director who trusts negative space completely.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; a flush 3-or-4-portrait concept-photo strip bleeds edge-to-edge across the top 58% of the slide with zero inter-column gutters between member photos. The lower 42% is a clean type zone with outer margins of roughly 8%; the album title sits oversized and centered within it. Dual-script group name — Hangul line directly above Latin line — is centered just above the album title, both lines sharing identical optical weight with no size differential between scripts. A single line of tracked monospace text anchors the very bottom edge as a tracklist or catalog footer; no header band, no page number block.

examples.promptCore: The slide inhabits the interior spread of a high-end idol photobook — cool, blue-shifted whitespace makes silence feel deliberate rather than empty. The concept-photo grid reads like a fashion editorial pull-out: images tight-cropped and luminous, carrying emotional weight while surrounding text stays spare and precise. Dual-script labeling treats both writing systems as equal visual objects, generating a typographic rhythm that feels bilingual by design rather than by accommodation. Avoid warmth, decorative ornamentation, or any layout gesture that signals corporate presentation over art direction.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 3–4 member concept-photo strip spanning full width across the upper two-thirds, separated by hairline gutters between frames. Below the photo band, Hangul and Latin romanization stack at matched cap-height across cols 2–11, neither script optically subordinate to the other. A tracked monospace tracklist or annotation line anchors the bottom edge as a footer rule, with a concept-code or page token sitting flush bottom-right. Side margins breathe at approximately 6–8%; the photo strip carries zero top bleed for a booklet-spread feel.
